case: A 62-year-old man with hypertension and hyperlipidemia presents with sudden vertigo, diplopia, slurred speech, and difficulty walking. He becomes progressively drowsy. Exam shows dysarthria, bilateral limb ataxia, and impaired horizontal eye movements.

case: A 45-year-old woman reports three weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea and dry cough. Chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy. Serum ACE is elevated.

case: A 58-year-old man with a history of diabetes presents with painless right eye vision loss over 2 days. Fundoscopy reveals new vessel growth on the optic disc.
clinical_question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
